newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan renews corn-buying collectives for 3 years.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan renews corn-buying collectives for 3 years.

text.p: Taiwan's Fair Trade Commission on Wednesday extended the operating authority of the island's two corn-buying groups for three years after a regular review found no anti-competitive practices, grain traders said.
The commission approved applications by the Members Feed Industry Group and the FGEP group to extend their collective buying practices to February 2000.
Such collective buying arrangements, designed to obtain better import prices, are subject to regular review by the commission to prevent market manipulation or price-fixing.
Traders said the commission found no illegal practices during the routine review.
The MFIG's main buyers are Taiwan's Formosa Oilseed, Fomau Cereal, Morn Sun Feed Mill and Shin Tai Industry.
The FGEP group comprises Fwu Sow Grain, Great Wall Enterprise, President Enterprise, Ever Smile Feed Mill Co and Fong Yu Co.
Taiwan imported 5.983 million tonnes corn, mainly from the United States, during 1996, traders said.
